elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "TrueLink shall defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates against any third-party claim..." — express defend obligation running to Client and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence: "shall defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates against any third-party claim".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (i): "alleging that the Interface, any related software, the Hosting Services or the Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — tracks the agreement's deliverable/service nouns.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (ii): "arising out of TrueLink's breach of applicable law".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or Credit Data caused by TrueLink" — Vendor-caused unauthorised access/disclosure of the Customer-side data categories used in this agreement.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Client shall give TrueLink prompt written notice of any claim indemnified under this Section 12".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "Client shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (iv): "arising out of TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Rendered 12(a)(i) still reads "any claim arising out of or relating to the Web Site or Client Content". The retained standalone "the Web Site or" hook is broader than Customer-provided content and, read literally, can still capture the very product/service injury and site-operation claims the drafter deleted from old limb (iv); the indemnity is therefore not "limited to" content plus Client's breach of law. Limb (ii) ("any breach by Client of any applicable state or federal law, rule or regulation") does satisfy the breach-of-law half.

reasons: Preferred level is one element short: the narrowed Client indemnity in 12(a)(i) retains the broad "the Web Site or" trigger. Repair by deleting "the Web Site or" so limb (i) reads "any claim arising out of or relating to Client Content (including any content posted to the Web Site by Client or Client's employees, agents or any customer of Client granted access to the Interface by Client)"; otherwise the deleted product/service-injury exposure re-enters through the Web Site hook and the indemnity is not limited to Customer-provided content.

Fallback level is not reached either: the insertion contains no procure/modify/replace remedy, no refund of applicable fees where those remedies are unavailable, and no 3x annual-fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity. The permissive exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) are optional at fallback, so their absence is not a defect, but the two mandatory remedy elements and the super-cap are missing. If the fallback is ever taken, those three items must be drafted expressly.

All other preferred elements are met in operative language: defend-and-indemnify running to Client and affiliates, IP infringement/misappropriation of the Interface, related software, Hosting and Support Services, Vendor breach of law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of Client Content or Credit Data, Vendor gross negligence/willful misconduct, plus prompt written notice, Vendor control of defence and settlement, and reasonable cooperation.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a concise addition of a missing Vendor indemnity, adds no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories or boilerplate, and the deletions inside 12(a) (breach-of-agreement limb, System/Credit Repository default limb, product-injury limb and the knowledge-qualifier override) are all necessary to reach the Customer-indemnity narrowing element. The existing 12(b) Vendor indemnity for breach/non-performance is retained rather than replaced.

Intent is preserved: the new paragraph sits inside Section 12 and does not disturb the liability cap (which by its terms applies to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11), the existing 12(b) indemnity, or any other allocation. One drafting check: confirm "Credit Data" is a defined term in this agreement ("Client Content" plainly is); if it is not, replace it with the defined data term to avoid a dangling reference.

Severity remains critical at this stage: as executed, the contract still has no Vendor IP indemnity, which is walk-away territory, and the proposed redline is not yet position-complete at either level.
